==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Http&min=Http&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Verify.Http: requests, responses, headers and content are written as readable snapshots,
        // and calls made while a recording is running are appended under the name httpCall.
        // Called explicitly so it runs before Verify.Flurl, which initializes Verify.Http itself
        // when it has not already run; a later VerifyHttp.Initialize() throws "Already Initialized".
        VerifyHttp.Initialize();

        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/HttpTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Http&min=Http&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using VerifyTests.Http;

// Verify.Http: Snapshots http requests and responses, records what an HttpClient sent, and ships a mock HttpClient.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Http
// Note: Recorded http entries are named httpCall; Recording.IgnoreNames("http") matches nothing.
// Note: The readme's HttpRecording.StartRecording() does not exist; the API is Recording.Start()
// from Verify core.
// Note: Nothing is captured unless a recording is running, so Recording.Start() has to run before
// the code under test makes its calls.
// Note: MockHttpClient can also replay files, new MockHttpClient("sample.html", "sample.json"),
// with the files copied to the output directory.
// Note: MockHttpHandler has the same constructors, for when the handler rather than the client has
// to be injected.
// Note: The package targets net10.0 only.
public class HttpTests
{
    // MockHttpClient answers every request without touching the network, so the test is
    // deterministic. The response is verified as status, headers and content.
    [Fact]
    public async Task MockResponse()
    {
        using var client = new MockHttpClient("the response", "text/plain");

        var result = await client.GetAsync("https://fake/get");

        await Verify(result);
    }

    // Every call made between Recording.Start() and the verification is added to the snapshot
    // under the name httpCall, so nothing has to be passed to Verify.
    [Fact]
    public async Task RecordCalls()
    {
        using var client = new MockHttpClient(recording: true);
        Recording.Start();

        await client.GetAsync("https://fake/get");

        await Verify();
    }
}
